seoTitle: How to Follow Up with a PhD Supervisor Who Hasn't Replied
title: How to Follow Up with a PhD Supervisor Who Hasn't Replied
content:
An unanswered email can mean many things, from workload to a closed recruitment cycle. Send a short follow-up that adds useful context, then continue exploring other suitable supervisors and projects.

Make the follow-up useful

Reply in the original email thread after a reasonable interval, taking account of the advertised deadline and any stated absence. Briefly remind the reader of the project and your relevant experience. Ask one question they can answer quickly, such as whether they expect to recruit for that intake.

Keep the message short

A possible message is: Dear Professor [Name], I am following up on my email about [specific project]. My experience in [relevant method] connects to your work on [topic]. Could you let me know whether you are considering doctoral applicants for [intake]? Thank you for your time. Replace every placeholder with accurate details.

Continue your search

Avoid sending repeated messages across several channels. Some programmes require a central application and do not expect an advance supervisor reply. Read the programme instructions, meet the formal deadline and continue exploring other groups whose research fits your preparation.

A follow-up should not become a new application

Keep the subject and original thread so the supervisor can see the context. Add only information that changes the request, such as an advertised vacancy you have now identified. Do not attach a larger collection of documents simply because the first message was unanswered. If the programme uses a central application, follow that route on time. A reply can help clarify research fit, but silence is not a decision on a formal application. Set a sensible point at which you continue with other suitable groups instead of repeatedly seeking a response.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review E5 NERC Doctoral Training Partnership at University of Edinburgh 2027. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.

You can also browse The University of Edinburgh on NextApply and the doctoral training programmes category. Listings and recruitment windows can change.

For the next part of your preparation, read How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips, After a PhD Rejection: Review Your Application and Plan Your Next Steps.
